title: Inventory Value does not move when an internal work order closes
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location has no accounting integration (neither QuickBooks Online nor AccountingHub).
  • Make sure Require Review Before Completion is off in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, in status Complete, with one approved line with one stock part picked from inventory at a cost of $40.00 each, quantity 2.
  • Open Reports > Inventory Value and note its total.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Click Close Work Order in the work order header.
  3. Click Close Work Order in the confirmation.
  4. Open Reports > Inventory Value.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The confirmation opens.

Step 3:

  • The work order is Closed.

Step 4:

  • The total is the noted figure: the parts left stock when they were picked.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11760 (Story 3, Close an internal or no-charge work order), story SV-11766 (Story 9, Reports, dashboard and exports)

  • S9-R9: “Inventory Value, Work In Progress and A/P reports are unchanged; an open internal or no-charge work order shows in Work In Progress with its badge and no value.”
  • Key Decisions: “Under the hood, Close creates an invoice marked internal or no charge. The screen says Closed · Internal or Closed · No Charge.”
